clue.text: Neglect odd parts of poem, lines showing blunder with words

parts.note: to neglect something is to miss it out

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters (first, third) of the word poem are taken

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a poet skimps on parts of a poem and makes a verbal gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd parts of' takes P and E, the first and third letters of 'poem'.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the letters of a word wrong is a blunder made with words.

clue.text: Ace intro for sales pitch

indicators.note: the intro, or opening, of the word sales is its first letter

parts.note: pitch is the black sticky substance tar

explanation.surface: A top salesperson's opening patter to a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' looks like an adjective describing the pitch, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is someone outstanding at something, a synonym for a top performer.

clue.text: For Les Bleus, a victory followed by day to chill out

parts.note: Les Bleus is the French national side, so 'a' in their language is un
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: The French team win and take a day off to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: Les Bleus is the nickname of France's national football and rugby teams, signalling French: their word for 'a' is UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is to relax after tension, as one does when chilling out.

clue.text: Simple man's abandoned without pity

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so these letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: someone without pity is heartless
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A simple fellow has been deserted by someone pitiless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man's abandoned' means the man (HE) has been dropped from HEARTLESS, which is 'without pity'.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means natural and unsophisticated, the same as simple or guileless.

clue.text: Material for building awfully dreamy team up

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of dreamy are badly arranged
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, reversed

parts.note: a team of eleven is written XI in Roman numerals, as for a cricket side

explanation.surface: Construction material for a team that has dreamed up a building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' signals the anagram of 'dreamy' and 'up' reverses the team of eleven, in a down clue read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-mixed concrete delivered to a site is a building material.

clue.text: Note celebrities eschewing ostentation

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A remark that famous people avoid showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: A minimalist style uses the fewest elements, so it avoids showiness and display.

clue.text: Saintly carpenter's record breaking banter

indicators.note: breaking into means one word splits the other open

parts.note: to josh is to tease or banter
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A holy woodworker's gramophone disc interrupts some teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Joseph, husband of Mary, was a carpenter by trade in the Gospels.

clue.text: Sort of gun in story by right bugger?

indicators.note: the gun sits in the story, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A tale of a gun beside a right-wing troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bugger?' is a cryptic definition: one who plants a bug, a hidden microphone, to eavesdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bugging a room is eavesdropping, in effect a hidden listener.

clue.text: Journalist's rubbish papers English rejected

indicators.note: rejected suggests being sent back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: A reporter's nonsense papers are turned down by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses ROTIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a senior newspaper journalist who prepares copy.

clue.text: Guardian with head of state, one on horse?

parts.note: the clue appears in the Guardian, so the paper speaking of itself is us
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was Britain's head of state

explanation.surface: A guardian accompanies the head of state while someone rides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' is this paper referring to itself as US; 'horse' is slang for heroin, so one on horse is a drug taker.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is slang for heroin, and a drug taker is called a user.

clue.text: 24 boy taken in by devil is wicked

indicators.note: taken in by means one piece is held inside another
wicked suggests the letters behave badly and get jumbled

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy is seduced by a devil who is truly evil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' rearranges DEVIL IS round LAD. The definition '24' points to 24-across, RASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash decision is ill-advised, unwise and hasty.

clue.text: Support many steady moves to cross road

indicators.note: to cross here means the jumbled letters straddle the other word, which goes inside
moves suggests the letters change position

parts.note: a path is a way or road

explanation.surface: A lot of people move steadily over a road to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges MANY STEADY, and 'to cross' places PATH within them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means comfort and kindness offered to someone in distress, a form of emotional support.

clue.text: Girl with old party skirt's accompaniment for date?

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
a do is a party
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A girl at an old-style party wears a skirt for a romantic date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' here is a year, not an outing: AD accompanies dates.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, abbreviated AD, follows a year to mark it in the Christian era.

clue.text: See 12
What Newgate is for Dickens

definitions.meaning: Newgate was a London prison, now gone
the dickens is a mild word for the devil

explanation.surface: How the novelist regarded the famous London prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a nickname for the Devil, and also describes a former prison.

clue.text: Person taking land cut kind of irrigation, by the way

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: colonic irrigation is a bowel-cleansing treatment
St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A settler trims back an irrigation scheme beside the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the final C from COLONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist settles new territory, often taking land from those already there.

clue.text: Inactive and without colour, having caught cold

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: having caught means one piece holds the other

parts.note: a tint is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone lies idle and pale after catching a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct volcano is no longer active, so the word means inactive.

clue.text: Strike through ball from the wing, like a striker

parts.note: in football a cross is a ball played in from the wing
a worker on strike is out

explanation.surface: A football commentary: a striker takes a ball crossed from the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' looks like a footballer, but here it is a worker on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike through words is to delete them with a line, the same as cancelling them.

clue.text: Articles with weight showing what litotes is for TS Eliot?

definitions.text: what litotes is for TS Eliot?

parts.note: an and a are both indefinite articles
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Pieces of writing show how a poet uses understatement.
explanation.walkthrough: LITOTES has the same letters as TS ELIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is a rearrangement of the letters of another, as the device here demonstrates.

clue.text: A learner admitted to periodical study in Oxford college

parts.note: a mag, magazine, is a periodical

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside

parts.note: a den is a study
L is the learner sign

explanation.surface: A student is let into the periodicals room at an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalen, pronounced 'maudlin', is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Settle a match, perhaps

parts.note: a match is one example of something that gives a light

explanation.surface: Resolve a sporting fixture, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a sporting contest, but it is the thing struck to make a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird settling on a branch alights on it: both verbs mean come down and rest.

clue.text: Two lots of gold rings extremely tough for creator

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold and or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: extremely means the outer letters of tough are taken

explanation.surface: Treasures in gold surround something tough for their maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' is the containment signal: the two gold pieces encircle the outer letters of 'tough'.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is the originator of something, its creator or maker.

clue.text: 10 to do arithmetic with new technology?

parts.note: to add is to do arithmetic
ICT is information and communication technology

explanation.surface: Using new technology for sums.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition '10' points to 10-across, USER.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is a habitual drug user, someone dependent on a substance.

clue.text: Small chap, following big road over the hill, ran badly

indicators.note: following means the small chap comes after the big road

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's major motorway, written MI
a man is a chap
over the hill means old, aged

explanation.surface: A small man trails along a motorway past the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, read as MI, is Britain's main north-south motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To mismanage something is to run it badly, past tense here.

clue.text: Outbreak of terror as hostage's grabbed

indicators.note: grabbed means the letters are held within the words

explanation.surface: A wave of terror as a hostage is seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbed' holds the letters across terroR AS Hostage.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak of spots on the skin is a rash.

clue.text: Thrash troublemaker's bottom in the open

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: something out is in the open, revealed

explanation.surface: Give a troublemaker a spanking outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' takes the last letter, R, of 'troublemaker'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rout an opponent is to defeat them heavily, to thrash them.

clue.text: I appreciate that Hollywood actor wants the Order of Merit

indicators.note: wants means lacks, so letters are removed

parts.note: Tom Hanks is a Hollywood film star
OM is the abbreviation for the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A grateful line to a film star who would like a British honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' means lacks, not desires.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'I appreciate that' is a way of expressing gratitude.

clue.text: Bow before short performance by American 2

parts.note: a bow is a curve, an arc

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a turn is a stage act or performance

explanation.surface: A bow taken before a brief act by an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts N from TURN. The definition '2' points to 2-down, STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcturus is the brightest star in the northern constellation Boötes.
